objective:
=== Goal ===
Objective: As Sol, inventory every open item in tracker/dotfiles-drift-remediation/, turn the inventory into precise agent-ready work packages, and orchestrate Luna/Terra implementation through verified completion with durable, resumable tracking.

Success criteria:
- All 53 currently unchecked entries are listed by original ID, reconciled against the current repository, and mapped to implementation, decision, or verification tasks without omissions or duplicate ownership.
- Each work package specifies its outcome, allowed files, exclusions, dependencies and decision gates, acceptance criteria, exact verification commands or fixtures, assigned model and supported thinking effort, and required handoff evidence.
- Approved remediation is implemented by delegated agents, reviewed by Sol, and covered by applicable checks. Decisions and maintainer review are explicit; blocked or skipped items are never reported as completed.
- Tracking records include task status, agent ownership, commits, checks and results, blockers, and next actions. A fresh Sol session can resume from repository records without needing this conversation.
- Work is committed on a new branch in a new worktree, then pushed to the repository remote after completion. The original checkout and its existing Pi settings and zsh edits remain untouched.

Boundaries:
- In scope: the tracker’s remaining privacy, WezTerm, Unix configuration delivery, setup safety, Krew/legacy cleanup, documentation, and integration work, plus coordination artifacts needed to delegate and resume it.
- Sol owns inventory, scoping, scheduling, decision requests, review, task tracking, checkpointing, and integration coordination. Sol may edit coordination records and run read-only inspections and verification commands; implementation and implementation-related documentation edits belong to delegated agents.
- Out of scope: unrelated refactors, incorporating pre-existing local edits, live host provisioning without approval, Windows-to-WSL copying, automatic history rewriting, force-pushing, and opening a pull request unless separately requested.

Constraints:
- Create an isolated new worktree and branch from the recorded committed baseline before edits or agent dispatch; do not copy unrelated uncommitted changes into it.
- Use Luna/Terra for implementation with high/highest thinking effort supported by the selected model. Verify actual model identities, effort support, and delegation tooling before dispatch; do not silently substitute Sol or another model. Ask the user if the requested setup is unavailable.
- Resolve DEC-001 through DEC-005 with the maintainer before dependent implementation. DEC-005 can record exclusion of the existing Pi edit through worktree isolation if the maintainer confirms that satisfies the decision. Also preserve the existing zsh edit.
- Follow repository instructions: Unix repository links through GNU Stow only; repository files remain canonical; Windows synchronization remains allowlisted and one-way; no credentials or machine-local data in tracked artifacts or agent reports.
- Assign exclusive file ownership or serialize work packages that touch the same files. Agents may not modify Sol-owned tracking records. Shared playbook, Windows setup, and wiki changes require ordered handoffs and review.
- Allow verified, explicitly staged local commits containing only authorized changes. Push only the completed new branch to the existing intended remote, without force. Any historical-data treatment needing a rewrite requires separate explicit authorization and an amended execution plan.
- Write checkpoints before dispatch, after agent handoff and verification, at blockers, and before context exhaustion. Record outstanding agent runs and integration state so a resumed session does not duplicate work.

Verification contract:
- Sol checks agent diffs against allowed scope and acceptance criteria before accepting completion.
- Require focused fixtures for synchronization direction, Stow conflict backup preservation/idempotency, unsupported Linux rejection, missing-command aggregation, and configuration target paths where applicable.
- Run Ansible syntax checks; wiki unit tests, audit, and changed-path responsibility validation across the full remediation range; relevant shell/PowerShell/configuration validation; package-specific and final Stow dry-runs; git diff --check; and a sanitized review for sensitive or machine-local content.
- Do not run setup against the live host merely to obtain evidence. Prefer temporary HOME/destination fixtures and non-mutating checks.
- Record unavailable platform checks with their reason and required follow-up. Obtain maintainer acceptance for outstanding platform-validation limitations and FIN-010 before claiming full completion or pushing the completed branch.

If blocked: Pause the affected task, write a resumable checkpoint describing the blocker and exact next action, and ask the user. Continue only independent, already-approved tasks. Never infer maintainer decisions, bypass failing checks, or claim blocked/skipped work passed.
